text: Attempt 12: attempt 11's start (proven) with the seaport, factory land and 7-8% taxes brought forward ~10 years, at most 4 loans. Loop now also stops on LAND short and spare water/power under 10%.
Day one ($15,764, attempt 11's plan a11-day1): 288 home tiles, shops, factories, coal plant, 2 fire stations, 12 pumps, road + rail links. Build check and audit passed.

Attempt 11 ended at 20,790 (2020). The reflection across all eleven attempts: every stall at 11-18k came with rising unemployment, the seaport fixed it, and 8% tax held. Attempt 12 replays attempt 11's start and moves those fixes ten years earlier.
Loan #2 ($10,000), allowed in Apr 2002 (a year earlier than attempt 11).
Blocks 3 + 4 ($7,647, plan a12-2003): +395 home tiles, east factory strip, shops. Second coal plant + 5 riverbank pumps ($4,614) built before the shortage this time.
Loan #3 ($10,000). Taxes 4/4/3 -> 7/7/7 at 6,090 people (rule: ~5,000; attempt 11 showed homes hold at 8% when jobs exist).
Seaport + 19 north riverbank pumps ($6,046) - the seaport 11 years earlier than attempt 11. East shop block (attempt 10's block 5, $2,196): 170 shop + 102 home tiles; shop land was short.
Jul 2003: 6,090 people, on the target curve for the first time in any attempt (attempt 11 had 3,710 at this date). Cash $1,800 after the seaport and shops; 3 of 4 loans used.
